codeReview.summary: The feature adds context/color/filter/help-version coverage and substantial tests, but two blocking parity bugs remain in file-filter regex error handling and context rendering on non-UTF8 input.

issues.description: Invalid `-G/--file-search-regex` values are silently ignored (`if let Ok(file_re) = Regex::new(file_re_str)`), causing parity break in diagnostics/exit semantics. Evidence: `./ag --nocolor -G "[" hello README.md` exits 2 with `ERR: Bad regex...`, while `target/debug/rust-ag --nocolor -G "[" hello README.md` exits 1 with empty stderr.

Context output uses `std::fs::read_to_string` and returns early on decode failure, so non-UTF8 files can match but emit no context lines. Evidence: `/tmp/ag_nonutf8.txt` with bytes `hello\n\xffworld\n`; `./ag --nocolor -A1 hello /tmp/ag_nonutf8.txt` prints `1:hello` and `2-...`, while `target/debug/rust-ag --nocolor -A1 hello /tmp/ag_nonutf8.txt` exits 0 with empty stdout.
Test coverage for `-G` is positive-path only and uses UTF-8 fixtures, so invalid-regex and non-UTF8 context parity regressions were not detected.

sharedStateObservations.observation: CLI formatting parity coverage does not include invalid `-G` regex behavior, which allowed a diagnostics/exit-class mismatch to ship.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: manifests/scenarios.json:358-367 defines only a valid `-G "\.rs$"` scenario; rust-ag/tests/parity_cli_context_color_filters.rs:404-422 tests only valid `-G` filtering.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Context fixture strategy is UTF-8-only; byte-oriented/non-UTF8 context behavior is not represented in shared parity tests despite baseline being byte-tolerant.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: rust-ag/tests/parity_cli_context_color_filters.rs:67-93 creates context fixtures via UTF-8 string writes only; no byte fixture for context-mode rendering.

summary: Review failed due to two blocking parity defects: invalid `-G` regex handling does not match baseline error semantics, and context output drops for non-UTF8 files. Feature coverage is otherwise substantial, but current tests/scenarios missed these edge cases.
